name: hover-does-not-seek
description: Moving the pointer across the timeline previews a position but never seeks - only a press and release moves playback.

steps.note: Pause first, so any movement below is caused by the pointer and not by playback.
Hover the far end of the timeline with no button held. RangeSlider tracks a hover fraction separately from its value, so this must move nothing.
And hover the near end, so the assertion covers a sweep in both directions rather than one resting position.
Bounded settle so any seek a hover wrongly started would already have landed before the core is read.

assertions.note: The control did not follow the pointer. A build that commits on hover would sit at 0.8 and fail here.
And the core did not move either. This is the assertion that matters: a hover that sought would send a viewer to a random point in the film just by moving the pointer across the dock.
